name: @eo/desktop
//productName: Electron prefers productName over name for app.getName(), which is what userData is derived from. Without it a packaged build stores its database under ~/.config/@eo/desktop — a stray `@eo` directory named after the workspace package, not the app.
//repository: electron-builder reads this to work out where `pnpm release` publishes; without it the release build warns and has no target.

scripts.//build:server: The organisation server's bundle (EO-319). Separate from `build` on purpose — see vite.server.config.ts — and run after it, because it leaves the workspace packages external the way the main bundle does.
scripts.//rotate:server-secrets: The admin's key rotation (EO-320). The same binary as `start:server`, which reads `--rotate-secrets` before anything else and re-encrypts every stored value under a new key instead of serving. It wants EO_SERVER_DATA, the current key and EO_SERVER_NEW_SECRET_KEY(_FILE); see src/main/server/rotateCommand.ts.
scripts.//start:server: Named `start:server` and not `server`, which is what it was: `pnpm server` is pnpm's own store-server command, so `pnpm --filter @eo/desktop server` never reached this script at all — it reached pnpm's, which rejected `--filter` with `Unknown option: 'recursive'`. A colon cannot collide, because every pnpm command is a single word. See server/launch.test.ts, which holds every script in this file to that rule.
scripts.typecheck: tsc -p tsconfig.node.json --noEmit && tsc -p tsconfig.preload.json --noEmit && tsc -p tsconfig.web.json --noEmit
scripts.//lint: Through `node` with an explicit heap, rather than the bare `eslint .` this was. Type-aware linting holds four TypeScript programs in one process at once -- one per tsconfig this app has, for `src/main`, `src/preload`, `src/renderer` and `e2e` -- and the peak is a little under 2 GB. Node's default heap is not a constant: it is sized from the memory the process can see, so a 15 GB workstation gets about 2.1 GB and a CI container gets whatever its cgroup allows, which is less. That is how `pnpm lint` passed on every machine anyone tried it on and then aborted with `Reached heap limit` in CI, on a branch whose only crime was being a few hundred lines long: the need had been sitting within a couple of hundred megabytes of the default for a while and nothing said so out loud. This says it out loud. Verified by bisecting the limit on `main` as well as on the branch that hit it -- both abort at 1536 MB and both finish at 2144 -- so the number is the repository's requirement rather than one story's. The lasting fix is fewer programs, which typescript-eslint's project service builds lazily; that is a change to how every package lints and a decision for somebody who is not chasing a red build.
scripts.//e2e: Builds first, and that is not belt-and-braces. Playwright launches `out/main/index.js`, so `playwright test` on its own tests whatever was last built — which on a branch means it can pass against code from before the change and report that the suite is green. That happened: a contract change whose whole risk was a module-load failure was declared verified by a suite that never loaded it. CI is unaffected (ci.yml builds through turbo and then calls `playwright test` directly); this is for everyone running it by hand, and `electron-vite build` costs about five seconds.
scripts.//postinstall: Deliberately absent. It was `electron-rebuild -f -w better-sqlite3`, and the `-f` is the whole problem: it compiles from source unconditionally, which needs a full C++ toolchain. That is the very failure the root package.json keeps better-sqlite3 out of `onlyBuiltDependencies` to avoid — on a machine without Visual Studio, `pnpm install` dies with "Could not find any Visual Studio installation to use" and exits non-zero. It survived because CI is Linux-only, where a toolchain happens to be present and the rebuild quietly succeeds. Nothing needs it: better-sqlite3 ships N-API prebuilds for every platform this app targets, and N-API is ABI-stable across both Node and Electron. Verified on Windows with an empty `build/` — better-sqlite3 opens a database and runs a query under Electron 39 (Node 22.22.1, ABI 140) on the prebuild alone. `@electron/rebuild` stays a devDependency: it is the mitigation for an Electron major bump, which is a deliberate act rather than an install hook.
